We get $2\times 5=10$ pieces in total.

q-59841.name: Question 6
q-59841.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14129499/assets/6463c24cede2d72af4574e9bc1ed15d09d6257e0a4e3393e52f74eddf874f862.png)

Each of the two shapes in the model above represents one whole. From left to right, what numbers are missing from the division problem below?

$$
\boxed{\,\,}÷\frac{1}{2}=\boxed{\,\,}
$$
q-59841.worked_solution:
In the model, there are $2$ shapes. Each shape consists of $2$ pieces that each represent $\frac{1}{2}$ of a whole. There are $4$ pieces in total.

The model tells us that when we divide $2$ wholes into halves, we will be left with $4$ pieces.

Hence, the division problem is:

$$
\boxed{\,2\,}÷\frac{1}{2}=\boxed{\,4\,}
$$

Therefore, the missing numbers are $2$ and $4.$
